chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

Four men testified against a muhsan man for adultery, two of whom were considered just (mu'tadal) and the other two were not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are four Muslims who are not known for perjury, their testimony is accepted in its entirety, and the hadd punishment is established against the one against whom they testified. They are only required to testify to what they saw and knew, and it is upon the ruler to accept their testimony unless they are known for moral corruption (fisq).'

key_terms.مُحْصَن: A free, adult Muslim who is not a slave, often implying he has had consummated marriage

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting testimony of four witnesses in an adultery case according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies the standard for witness justice (adal) in hudud cases, distinguishing between general moral corruption (fisq) and specific perjury (shahadat al-zur). It emphasizes that the ruler's acceptance is presumed unless the witnesses are publicly known for corruption, ensuring that the hadd punishment is applied based on direct observation rather than rigid uniformity of all four witnesses' status.
